title: 1995 AMC 8 Problem 15
statement: What is the \(100\)th digit to the right of the decimal point in the decimal form of \(\dfrac{4}{37}?\)

solutions.text:
\(\dfrac{4}{37} = 0.\overline{108},\) repeating with block length \(3.\) The digits in positions \(3,\) \(6,\) \(9,\) \(\ldots\) (multiples of \(3\)) are \(8.\)

Since \(99\) is a multiple of \(3,\) the \(99\)th digit is \(8,\) so the \(100\)th digit starts the next block: it is \(1.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B .
hints: Write \(\dfrac{4}{37}\) as a repeating decimal and find the length of the repeating block
The block has length \(3;\) use the remainder of \(100\) divided by \(3\)
